mediaWork.title: Scenes of a Crime
mediaWork.focusOrTheme: Examines the lengthy police interrogation of Adrian Thomas in Troy, New York, which resulted in a disputed confession regarding the death of his infant son. Critiques interrogation techniques and explores the phenomenon of false confessions.
mediaWork.summaryNotes: A father is interrogated for 11 hours until he confesses to a crime he says he didn't commit. This documentary explores the science of interrogation and false confessions.

mediaItems.focusOrTheme: Examines the lengthy police interrogation of Adrian Thomas in Troy, New York, which resulted in a disputed confession regarding the death of his infant son. Critiques interrogation techniques and explores the phenomenon of false confessions.
mediaItems.summaryNotes: The documentary features extensive footage from Adrian Thomas's actual videotaped interrogation, interviews with Thomas, his family, lawyers, and jurors. It analyzes the specific techniques used by police during the 10-hour questioning.

featuredIndividuals.narrativeSummary: Adrian Thomas was wrongfully convicted of second-degree murder in the death of his infant son. His conviction was based on a false confession obtained through coercive interrogation techniques. He was exonerated in 2014 after his confession was suppressed and his conviction was overturned.
